title: the anchor azimuth of a raster turn, derived on the lattice, and C-0201's 36-corner span bracket collapsed onto it
verificationType: logical (exact integer residue arithmetic on this repository's own honeycomb crossover lattice, a closed form for the azimuth, and C-0147's span geometry consumed unmodified) + in-silico (the same honeycomb grillage, the same tether element and the same 64 coupled cells C-0167, C-0180 and C-0201 share, re-run at the determined span) + literature (C-0152's allowed-crossover span, C-0200's duplex window, T-71's measured phosphate radius and T-230's ssDNA Kuhn and contour brackets)
maturity: TRL 1-3. Model-consistent and traceable. NOT empirically demonstrated. The azimuth is a property of a DESIGN -- the drawable 102 / 109 raster of the 10 x 6 block -- and not of a folded object; no folding experiment is reported and this repository cannot run one.

units.angle: degrees at every boundary of this study, radians only inside a trigonometric call
units.level: integer base pairs on one global z
units.dishing: dimensionless, as a fraction of the free stroke

conventions.azimuth: measured at helix a from the line of centres pointing at helix b, positive in the sense of increasing z at +240/7 deg per base pair; theta = 0 is closest approach and theta = 180 deg is furthest
conventions.the two anchors: at the SAME base-pair level. Both helices of a honeycomb bond are parallel, same-handed and at one design twist, so a level displacement rotates both backbones the same way and the entry azimuth is the exit azimuth plus 180 deg exactly
conventions.the exact facing residue: b0 + 21/4, not b0 + 5. caDNAno's rule is five base pairs OR HALF A TURN and the half turn at 10.5 bp/turn is 5.25 bp; because 10.5 bp is exactly 360 deg, b0 + 5.25 and b0 - 5.25 are ONE azimuth
conventions.the anchor reading: the raster's row lengths are PAIRED lengths and route B's unpaired loop sits OUTBOARD of the duplex, so the last paired base sits AT the raster level and anchorOffsetBasePairs is 0. That is C-0200's reading of the built block and C-0201 section 7's own width arithmetic
conventions.the turn census: honeycombRasterTurnList's, unchanged -- the same 59 sites route A uses, so the comparison with C-0175, C-0180 and C-0201 is controlled
conventions.the datum: AZIMUTH_PER_BASE_PAIR is +240/7 deg per base pair of INCREASING z, so it reverses whenever z does; a residue map is a handedness (CLAUDE.md)

parameters.whyTheRegimeBlockIsNull: environment.Regime holds the gap and the bias as INTERVALS and refuses a degenerate one; this study solves no electrostatics, it reads ONE profile record of T-3b and uses it as a fixed load shape, so the state is a POINT and belongs here rather than in a range (C-0181, CH-0224)
parameters.loopLengths: 15, 20 and 28 nt (C-0201's own set) plus C-0200's ordered 24 / 32
parameters.mandate: C-0017's 33.3333 pN/nm on the SUM, section 3's acceptable clause

sources: gpd/results/T-3b-tile-edge-load-profile.json (C-0022's solved collar at 2 mM / 10 nm / 0.192 V)

cheapBound.question: what fixes the span of route B's tether?
cheapBound.answer: the base-pair index of the last PAIRED base and the lattice phase, and nothing else. The chain leaves helix a at that base's phosphate and enters helix b at its own; both helices of a honeycomb bond are parallel, same-handed and at one design twist, so a level displacement rotates BOTH backbones the same way and one angle serves the pair
cheapBound.consequence: theta(rho, b0) = fold((rho - b0 - 21/4) x 240/7 deg) and span(theta) = sqrt(d^2 - 4 d r_P cos theta + 4 r_P^2). Fifty-nine turns, eight datum readings, no solver at all

cheapBound.question: and on the recommended raster, what is it?
cheapBound.answer: C-0187 pins b0 = 5 with residues [0, 10] on the drawable 102 / 109 raster, so every raster turn sits at an ALLOWED scaffold crossover and the anchor azimuth is C-0152's own quarter base pair, 8.57142857 deg
cheapBound.consequence: the span is 0.787091706 nm at all 59 turns -- 1.0951233x the aligned end of C-0201's bracket and 5.53083673x below its worst end. It is a number the corpus already carries, in T-246's own result file

cheapBound.question: why does the rim alternation not split it into two populations?
cheapBound.answer: because the span depends on cos(theta), which is EVEN. C-0187's derived departure is +8.57142857 deg at the high rim and its negation at the low one, and an anchor offset moves inboard at both rims, so the two rims' azimuths are exact negatives at every offset
cheapBound.consequence: one span, at every one of the 59 turns and at every anchor offset -- which is F1, declared open before the run, and it did not fire

cheapBound.question: does the collapse need the coupling bank re-solved?
cheapBound.answer: no. C-0201 establishes that the preload is C-0104's internal initial stress -- it changes no entry of the stiffness matrix and the field is exactly linear in it -- so pricing a DETERMINED span is a re-evaluation of an element whose machinery exists, at one span instead of three
cheapBound.consequence: C-0201's 36 corners fall to 16 and the coupled grade is a CHECK of a prediction rather than a search

offsets.reading: the built and graded reading: the loop sits OUTBOARD of the duplex

findings: THE SPAN IS NOT A BRACKET AND IT IS NOT UNKNOWN: on the recommended 102 / 109 raster every one of the 59 raster turns anchors at an ALLOWED scaffold crossover, so its two phosphates sit at 8.57142857 deg and 188.571429 deg from the line of centres and the tether's span is 0.787091706 nm -- ONE value, at all 59 turns and at all eight readings of the axial datum. It is C-0152's own allowed-crossover span, reproduced out of T-246's committed result file at a departure of 0.0.
